subject: Custom service commitment rider — order form language & evidence path
messages:
From: Evan Miller <evan.miller@arcadialabs.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@arcadialabs.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 12:42:00 -0400
Subject: Request: tailored SLA rider + evidence for enterprise MSA

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the demo last week — Arcadia is excited about Redwood's runtime performance. Procurement asked me to get a formal proposal for a tailored SLA exhibit to attach to our enterprise MSA. High-level asks: 99.99% availability across multi-region deployments (primary + failover), p95 token latency target of <=200ms for standard batching profile, and an operational evidence package describing monitoring, alerting, and incident timelines.

Specifically we need:
- A redlineable SLA addendum (rider) and the order form language we can insert into our PO flow.
- A short evidence/runbook bundle (what telemetry you can provide: token-level latency histograms, per-region uptime, audit logs) and a proposed DocuSign flow for the MSA + rider.
- Timeline: procurement would like a review copy by EOD Tuesday so legal can start redlines.

Are you able to share a draft rider and the expected evidence artifacts? If you can include a brief note about fallbacks (model variant fallback, burst protection) that helps our SREs.

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Miller
Head of Procurement | Arcadia Labs
Evan.Miller@arcadialabs.com
+1 415 555 0198
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Miller <evan.miller@arcadialabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 17:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: tailored SLA rider + evidence for enterprise MSA

Evan — thanks for the clear asks. Attaching an initial draft rider and two companion artifacts for review.

Attachments: arcadia_sla_rider_draft_v1.docx (docx), orderform_proposed_language_v1.pdf (pdf), evidence_runbook_outline.xlsx (xlsx)

Quick notes:
- Draft rider targets availability language and maps service credit schedule to monthly uptime percentage. We've left blanks for the agreed-upon p95 latency numbers and the SLO measurement windows so your legal can redline.
- Order form PDF includes language for dedicated vs hosted routing and a clause for automatic model-variant fallback if primary model is unavailable.
- Evidence runbook is an outline of telemetry we can provide (per-region uptime, aggregated p50/p95 latency buckets, token-level sample traces if needed) and recommended on-call escalation steps.

Internal owners: Ben (pricing & order form) — can you confirm the order form clause here is compatible with reserved capacity pricing? Karthik (legal/availability evidence) — please add any items we should include for compliance. Monica (CS lead for Arcadia onboarding) — can you draft a short operational note on typical warmup times and cache behavior for multi-region failover so Evan's SREs have an expectation?

Evan — I can get a cleaned up version back to you tomorrow morning. If procurement needs to see a sample DocuSign flow we can share a test envelope link.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
Aisha.Rahman@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 17:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: tailored SLA rider + evidence for enterprise MSA

Thanks for the draft — quick internal notes:

- Order form language: the dedicated routing language is okay but we should surface the burst protection clause (2x baseline throughput for 5 minutes) as an optional add-on rather than default. That keeps baseline price predictable.
- Credits: I'd keep the service credit ladder symmetrical to our standard exhibit but add a one-time remediation credit cap for network-level incidents outside our control.
- Evidence: we can deliver per-region uptime CSVs and p95 histograms weekly initially; token-level traces require a data access agreement — Karthik, we should confirm the redwood data sharing addendum for that.

I'll loop back with sample cost numbers for the optional burst protection by EOD.

-Ben

Subject: Re: Request: tailored SLA rider + evidence for enterprise MSA

Evan — following up with the updated items after internal review. Summary of changes and next steps: 

What we updated:
- Rider: clarified scope for multi-region failover, added explicit measurement window for availability (30-day rolling), and marked the p95 latency clause as an SLA target with a measurement method.
- Order form: pushed the burst protection to an opt-in item; added a short procurement-friendly clause for automatic fallback to compatible model variants when capacity constrained.
- Evidence bundle: we can publish per-region uptime CSVs, weekly p95/p50 latency histograms, and a runbook excerpt describing alert thresholds and incident timelines. Token-level traces will require a short data sharing addendum — attached a template for that.

Attachments: arcadia_sla_rider_draft_v1.docx (updated), orderform_proposed_language_v1.pdf (updated), evidence_runbook_outline.xlsx (updated), data_sharing_addendum_template.pdf

DocuSign & call:
- DocuSign: I created a test envelope to show the MSA + rider flow: https://docusign.com/arcadia/Envelope12345
- Proposed next step: 30-minute sync with Arcadia legal + SRE tomorrow at 10am PT to walk through the evidence artifacts and confirm redlines. Can you confirm availability?

If that works I'll open a DocuSign envelope for signatures after legal signs off.

Best,
Aisha
